articleTitle: A highly linearised mm-wave voltage controlled oscillator for FMCW radar applications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Solid State Components for Radar
abstract: The author describes a technique of frequency feedback by which the linearity of a voltage controlled Gunn effect oscillator may be improved from a natural value of around 10% to a linearised value of less than 1%. He includes a description of how the lineariser is constructed using quartz microstrips for the mm-wave elements and thick film hybrid techniques for low frequency components. Results of linearity measurements are represented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: GaAs MMIC phase shifters for phased arrays
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Solid State Components for Radar
abstract: The author describes the design of two types of four-bit phase shifter commonly used for phased array radar applications. The first phase shifter is a switched delay line type designed for operation over the band 2.7-3.3 GHz and is realised partially as a GaAs MMIC. The second phase shifter described is a switched filter type designed for operation over the band 4-8 GHz and will be realised wholly as a GaAs MMIC.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Solid State Components for Radar
abstract: The author discusses some new device geometries expected to extend the useful fundamental operating frequency range of GaAs two terminal transferred electron devices (TEDs) or Gunn elements beyond 100 GHz. Similar structures are studied for multi-layered GaAs MMW IMPATT devices. Local oscillator millimeter wave (MMW) systems are predominately IMPATT (high power) and Gunn (low noise) sources. These components have been realized in both waveguide and integrated circuit configurations throughout the most widely used portion (26.5-110 GHz) of the MMW region.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Recent investigations into W-band pulsed IMPATT oscillator design
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Solid State Components for Radar
abstract: The author reports on some of the experimental techniques used and results achieved during development work on W-band pulsed IMPATT oscillators. The particular application of these sources was to form an injection locked amplifier chain as part of a frequency agile data gathering radar. The oscillators were based on a modular waveguide cavity allowing for ease of construction and interchangeability. Diodes were silicon double-drift devices and were nominally centred on 94 GHz with various output powers between 1 W and 10 W.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A production oriented GaAs monolithic low noise amplifier for phased array radar systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Solid State Components for Radar
abstract: The design and performance of a two stage GaAs monolithic S-band low noise amplifier (LNA) is described. The design approach was aimed at realising a high performance, small size MMIC with good yields and low chip costs based around a 1 micron gate length MESFET IC technology. A negative feedback circuit topology was selected and optimised for minimum sensitivity to process batch variations, thus ensuring maximum yield. Practical results from the first production batches show that noise figures of less than 2.3 dB with more than 15 dB of associated gain have been realised simultaneously with input and output VSWRs of less than 2:1. These results are typical of the amplifier performances seen across several 2" wafer batches. However, noise figures as low as 2.0 dB have been measured.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distributed amplifiers as duplexer/circulator components at S-band
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Solid State Components for Radar
abstract: The signal flow characteristics of distributed amplifiers are studied, and it is found that such modules can be designed to suit certain solid-state duplexer/circulator or bi-directional amplifier applications. A module with a measured S/sub 31/ (transmit to receive) isolation of typically 10 dB is described, and found to have a gain of about 6.0 dB in the S/sub 34/ direction and 7.5 dB in the S/sub 21/ direction. A major motivation of this research is to seek all solid-state design solutions for low power FMCW radar and duplex communications equipment; thereby obviating the use of ferrite circulator components.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Solid State Components for Radar
abstract: The authors consider three different hardware implementations for carrying out digital pulse compression. The first is by direct convolution using commercially available signal processing components. The second is by fast convolution using a chip set designed for the efficient implementation of the FFT butterfly, while the third also implements fast convolution but using multiple single chip digital signal processors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Monolithic low noise amplifier-a foundry GaAs IC
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Solid State Components for Radar
abstract: The authors describe the development of a monolithic 4-6 GHz low noise amplifier for an application in phased array radar. The design rules were purchased from Plessey 3-5 Ltd. and the design and layout were carried out using standard CAD software. The resulting tape was delivered to the foundry where the chips were fabricated. The amplifier worked satisfactorily on the first design iteration giving over 15 dB of gain, less than 3.5 dB noise figure and matches of better than 2:1. The design procedure, and the measurements on the devices, are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A 2-6 GHz MMIC attenuator and 5-6 GHz MMIC vector modulator using segmented dual gate FETs
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Solid State Components for Radar
abstract: Microwave attenuators and phase shifters are key elements in phased array radar systems. In such applications they are required in large quantities per system which make them ideal candidates for monolithic technology. The author describes some initial results from devices designed by Thorn EMI and produced by a foundry (Plessey 3-5). The circuits are a 2-6 GHz 20 dB 6-bit attenuator using a segmented dual gate FET and a 5-6 GHz 22.5 degree resolution 90 degree vector modulator using segmented dual gate FETs and a highpass/lowpass phase shifter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
